stage_a.note: Both founders present with strong enthusiasm and smiles, maintaining an upbeat tone throughout.
Juls enthusiastically introduces the live dog demonstration, showing strong engagement with the product.
Carolyn warmly and gently handles the dog during the demonstration, showing an approachable orientation.

venture.description: A multifunctional car harness designed to keep small pets safe during car travel by securing them to the seat.
venture.note: The founders demonstrate the product using live dogs on stage.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founders introduce themselves and their pet safety harness, showing crash test footage of failed competitors.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Robert laughs loudly at the video of the dogs strapped into the car seats.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Juls acknowledges the funny appearance of the dogs in the video.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Kevin bursts into loud laughter at the sight of the dogs.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Robert jokes that the dog in the video looks really happy.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Juls admits the dogs look silly but asks the sharks to trust them on the safety aspect.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Lori points out that the panel is laughing too hard to hear the pitch.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Kevin expresses disbelief at the product and the dogs' positioning.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Robert expresses disbelief, saying they have to be kidding.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Juls continues the pitch and transitions to a live demonstration with one of their dogs.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Juls and Carolyn demonstrate how to strap the dog into the harness and secure it to the seat.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Kevin jokingly asks if drugs were involved in keeping the dog so calm.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Juls denies using drugs on the dog.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Lori notes the dog seems fine but questions how it can possibly be happy in that position.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Mark asks what the alternative product is for securing dogs in cars.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Kevin argues that dogs prefer to stick their heads out the window.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Juls finishes demonstrating how to adjust the straps to secure the dog.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Juls explains that suspending the dog above the seat protects its spine during travel.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Lori asks if the dog is scared while strapped into the harness.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Juls explains the dog is merely nervous due to the pitching environment, not the harness itself.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Carolyn shows a video of their product passing the crash test with perfect scores.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Juls highlights that the pack includes front and backpack attachments for carrying the dog outside the car.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Daymond expresses his approval of the additional carrier applications.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Lori compares the product's functionality to a baby carrier.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Robert compliments the idea behind the product.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Kevin asks if there are other similar products currently on the market.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Juls states they are the only such product and hold a patent.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Kevin challenges her claim, saying he has seen people strapping dogs to bikes.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Juls clarifies that those other products exist but are neither crash tested nor safety approved.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Mark asks for the retail price of the product.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Juls states the product costs one hundred and sixty dollars.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Robert remarks that the price is very expensive.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Mark asks for the manufacturing cost of the product.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Juls states it costs them thirty-six dollars to make.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Lori remarks that they have a huge profit margin.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Mark asks for their current sales figures.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Juls states they have one hundred eighty thousand dollars in sales since launching in November.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Mark asks where the products are being sold.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Juls states they only sell the product through their own website.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Mark asks how they drive traffic to their website.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Juls states their traffic is generated organically and through word of mouth.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Lori asks how they came up with the idea for the product.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Carolyn explains she developed and patented it to travel safely with her injured dog.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Juls explains she licensed the product from Carolyn because she strongly believes in the project.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Lori asks Juls how much money she invested into Carolyn's business.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Juls states she has invested two hundred thousand dollars altogether.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Robert asks what the invested money was spent on.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Juls explains the funds went into crash testing, production, and two hundred thousand dollars of inventory.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Daymond asks who manages the daily operations of the business.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Juls states that she runs the daily operations.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Lori asks what Carolyn's role in the business is.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Juls states that Carolyn handles all fulfillment from her garage.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Lori expresses mild surprise at the fulfillment arrangement.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Kevin asks Carolyn for data on the number of dogs killed yearly in car accidents.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Carolyn admits she doesn't know the exact number but mentions UK insurance laws regarding unsecured dogs.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Lori expresses surprise that such laws are actually being put into place.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Mark asks if they sell their products in the UK.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Juls confirms they sell in the UK and in forty different countries.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Kevin jokes that given their total sales, they must sell only one unit per country.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Juls laughs and thanks Kevin for his teasing remark.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Kevin clarifies that he is just dealing with her and teasing.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Juls deflects the sales challenge by emphasizing their crash test success and the large size of the pet industry.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Robert decides not to invest because he feels the product is too complicated and time-consuming to use.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Kevin exits because the business is too early and the valuation is too high.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Lori exits because the product looks too complicated and needs to be simplified.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Daymond decides not to invest because he feels it is too early and they haven't figured everything out.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Mark exits due to poor marketing, advising them to sell against fear rather than cuteness.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Juls thanks the sharks for their time.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Mark and the other sharks wish the founders good luck as they leave.

decisions.note: Product seems too complicated and takes too much time to use.
Business is too early and valuation is too high.
Product looks complicated and needs to be simpler to use.
Too early and they haven't figured everything out yet.
Poor marketing; they need to sell against fear rather than cuteness.
